Matrix Multiplication
Matrix multiplication is an operation in linear algebra that combines two matrices to produce a new matrix.
It involves taking the dot product of the rows of the first matrix with the columns of the second matrix and summing the results.
Let's see how it actually works.

When performing matrix multiplication, the rows of the first matrix are multiplied by the corresponding columns of the second matrix, and the results are summed up to form the elements of the resulting matrix.
To clarify, let's consider two matrices, A and B, where A has dimensions (2 x 2) and B has dimensions (2 x 2). The resulting matrix C, obtained by multiplying A and B, will have dimensions (2 x 2).
How does the multiplication process work?
Consider two 2x2 matrices A and B.
First, take the first row of matrix A and the first column of matrix B. Multiply the corresponding elements pairwise and sum them up.

blocks.alt: Matrix multiplication between first row of A and first column of B

blocks.content: This sum becomes the first element of the resulting matrix C.
Then, repeat the process for the remaining columns of matrix B, keeping the first row of matrix A fixed. Each calculation generates an element in the first row of matrix C.

blocks.alt: Matrix multiplication between first row of A and second column of B

blocks.content: Now, move to the next row of matrix A and repeat above steps until all rows of matrix A are processed. Each row of matrix A generates a corresponding row in matrix C.

blocks.alt: Matrix multiplication between second row of A and first column of B

blocks.content: Continue this process until all rows of matrix A are multiplied with all columns of matrix B. The resulting matrix C will have m rows and p columns.
